newsitem.title: USA: Universal Hospital says may sell company.
newsitem.headline: Universal Hospital says may sell company.

text.p: Universal Hospital Services Inc said on Monday its board of directors is exploring alternatives to enhance shareholder value, including the sale of the company.
The company said the board of directors received a letter from another company interested in acquiring UHS for "a range exceeding the current market price for UHS's common stock".

UHS has hired Piper Jaffray to act as its advisor and to manage the process. Included among the alternatives to be considered is the continued operation of the business as an independent company, UHS said.

"During this process, UHS will continue to provide the product quality and high level of service which have become the company's hallmark," said Thomas Minner, president and chief executive of UHS. "We remain committed to meeting the needs of our customers and vendors."

UHS said as a part of the plan, it adopted on November 8 a shareholder rights plan to encourage anyone seeking to acquire the company to negotiate with the board. Under the plan, shareholders receive a right to purchase a new series of preferred stock, exercisable if a person or group acquired 15 percent or more of the company's common stock.
Earlier this month, UHS reported third quarter earnings declined to $0.10 a share from $0.11 a share last year. It said it implemented several expense control initiatives.

UHS said net income declines were due to acquisition costs and the continuing decline in the sale of disposable supplies. At that time, the medical equipment supplier said it continues to experience declining sales of Demand Positive Airway Pressure devices and surplus inventories.
